content: 1. The enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of many drugs. When co-administering drugs metabolized predominantly by CYP3A4, dose adjustments may be necessary, and close monitoring is recommended. 2. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers, and monitor closely. 3. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of tazemetostat. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor closely. 4. Tecovirimat, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, reduces the levels or effects of efavirenz. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness when co-administered. 5. Efavirenz and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Telotristat ethyl reduces the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. Consider increasing the dosage of the interacting drug if necessary, and monitor closely. 7. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of temsirolimus, teniposide, and terbinafine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Efavirenz and tenofovir DF increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Efavirenz and tetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of tetracycline, tezacaftor, and theophylline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, and monitor closely. 11. Efavirenz and thiothixene both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of tiagabine and ticagrelor by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid ticagrelor with potent CYP3A inducers, and monitor closely. 13. Efavirenz and ticlopidine interact bidirectionally, affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of tinidazole, tipranavir, and tramadol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 15. Efavirenz and tipranavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tipranavir also increases efavirenz levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Efavirenz and trazodone both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension and triazolam by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Triazolam levels may also increase due to decreased metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Efavirenz and triclabenazole both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Efavirenz and trifluoperazine both decrease the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of trimipramine by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Efavirenz and triptorelin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of tucatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tucatinib also increases efavirenz levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Efavirenz reduces the effects of ublituximab due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of ubrogepant and ulipristal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs decrease the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 27. Efavirenz and valbenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Efavirenz reduces the effects of valoctocogene roxaparvovec due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 29. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of vandetanib, vardenafil, and velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of vemurafenib and venetoclax by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of venlafaxine and verapamil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Verapamil may increase efavirenz levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of vilazodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider increasing the vilazodone dose up to twofold, not exceeding 80 mg/day, when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers for more than 14 days. 34. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of vinblastine, vincristine, vincristine liposomal, and vinorelbine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 35. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of voclosporin and vonoprazan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Voriconazole increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz reduces voriconazole levels. This combination is contraindicated at efavirenz doses of 400 mg/day or higher. 38. Efavirenz and vorinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of vortioxetine by increasing metabolism. Consider increasing the vortioxetine dose when co-administered with strong CYP inducers for more than 14 days, not exceeding three times the original dose. 40. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 41. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of warfarin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 42. Zafirlukast increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 43. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of zaleplon by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 44. Efavirenz reduces the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, increase the zanubrutinib dose to 320 mg twice daily. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inducer.
